 --------RESPONDENTS __________________________________________________________ For the applicant : Mr. Aman Tamboli, Advocate For the Respondent/State : Ms. Shailja Shukla, Dy. GA
Hon'ble

Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 15/06/2024.
1.

The applicant has preferred this second bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail, as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 538/2023 registered at Police Station- Dongargarh District- Rajnandgaon (C.G.), for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
The first bail application was rejected on 09.02.2024 in MCRCA No. 58 of 2024.

2. Case of the prosecution, in brief is that the complainant has lodged complaint alleging that co-accused Sunil Patel, Rajesh Mahilange and other two persons for providing employment on the basis of fabricated documents had taken huge amount of Rs. 18,50,000/- from him.

On 19.10.2022,
they took 1,00,000/- in cash and thereafter, he transferred Rs. 10,00,000/- in the account of Rajesh Mahilange and Sunil Patel and given Rs. 2,00,000/- in cash.
On 18.11.2022 he received appointment letter through post in which he was asked to meet Howrah Divisional Railway Manager on 21.11.2022 at 10 am.
On 21.11.2022, Rajesh Mahilang took him to the office of the Divisional Railway Manger where he was given Service Book and an order copy for attending training.
From 28.11.2022 he was given training for 45 days at Wardhman by a person namely Dilip.

1 period, he paid Rs. 50,000/- in the account of one Rahul Sarkar, who was a Railway Officer and paid Rs. 5,00,000/- in cash, as such, he has been cheated for total amount of Rs. 18,50,000/-, this led him to lodge FIR.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that in the FIR name of the applicant has not been mentioned, his name has been recorded on the memorandum statement of Sukhendra Chandrakar.
He would further submit that amount of Rs. 15,00,000/- has already been returned to the complainant.

He would further submit that the main accused in the case has already settled their dispute with the victim and the victim and his father themselves have not supported the case of the prosecution and have turned hostile, therefore, would pray that applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and would submit that the applicant was the master mind of the crime.

To substantiate his submission he would draw attention of this Court towards the statement of the witnesses who have reiterated the same story which has been mentioned in the FIR, therefore the anticipatory bail application may kindly be rejected.
5. Counsel for respondent No.2 has filed no objection application wherein he has stated that he has no objection, if the applicant is released on bail.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the case diary.

7. Considering the fact that at the time of dismissal of first anticipatory bail application, statements of the complainants were not recorded now the circumstances has been changed and the statements of Yogesh Hirwani (PW-1) and his father Kacharu Hirwani (PW-2) were recorded wherein they have denied the fact that the applicant and other co-accused have cheated them and took Rs. 18,50,000/-
for getting employment in the Railway and both the witnesses have not supported the case of the prosectution and has turned hostile, I am inclined to grant benefit of Section 438 of CrPC to the applicant.
8.

Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is allowed and It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with the aforesaid offence, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail by the officer arresting on executing a personal bond in sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer.
